claims.statement: Ayrton Senna won the Drivers’ World Championship in 1988, 1990 and 1991 with McLaren.

evidence.locator: PDF page 80 (1-based), printed page 77, Drivers’ World Championship Winners table: 1988, 1990 and 1991 rows

claims.statement: The official 1988 Drivers’ Standings list Ayrton Senna first with 90 points and Alain Prost second with 87.

evidence.locator: 1988 Drivers’ Standings table, first two rows, Pos. / Driver / Pts. columns; championship table, not a sum of race-result points

claims.statement: On 3 June 1984 Ayrton Senna finished second at the Monaco Grand Prix for Toleman-Hart, behind winner Alain Prost.

evidence.locator: 3 June 1984 result, position 1 Prost / McLaren TAG and position 2 Senna / Toleman Hart

claims.statement: On 21 April 1985 Ayrton Senna won the Portuguese Grand Prix driving for Lotus-Renault.

evidence.locator: 21 April 1985 result, position 1 Senna / Lotus Renault

claims.statement: On 23 May 1993 Ayrton Senna won the Monaco Grand Prix driving for McLaren-Ford.

evidence.locator: 23 May 1993 result, position 1 Senna / McLaren Ford

claims.statement: Senna entered Formula 1 with Toleman in 1984, then moved to Lotus for 1985. His first world title came with McLaren in 1988.

evidence.locator: Career paragraphs: Toleman debut, Lotus move and first McLaren championship

claims.statement: After three seasons with Lotus, Senna raced for McLaren from 1988 through 1993 and joined Williams in 1994.

Gerald Donaldson’s Formula 1 retrospective presents Senna’s McLaren partnership with Alain Prost as a rivalry that extended into their championship contests at Suzuka in 1989 and 1990. This is an attributed retrospective account, not evidence of either driver’s intentions.

evidence.locator: McLaren/Prost rivalry and 1989–1990 Suzuka paragraphs; motives deliberately not adopted
